Vieksniai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Vieksniai produced an unusually large roster of notable natives: the Zionist leader Avraham Idelson; the Zionist activist Yehudah-Leib Apel; Miriam Shakh, who served as secretary to Theodor Herzl, founder of modern political Zionism, himself; her brother, the writer Fabius Shakh; the writer Yisrael Efroikin; the journalist Aharon-Yits'hak Grodzensky; and the writer Meir-Joel Vigoder. Communal life centered on the 'shulhoyf,' which housed the local yeshiva and two prayer houses, one for winter and one for summer. On August 4, 1941, guarded by armed Lithuanians, Vieksniai's Jews were transferred to Mazeikiai — the massive regional massacre site documented at length elsewhere in this collection — and herded to the Jewish cemetery there together with Mazeikiai's own Jews and those of neighboring towns, where all were shot the next day after being forced to dig their own graves.
